### Cyrus v5: the owner's redesign (2026-10-08, branch `feature/cyrus-v5`)

The owner's own Cyrus redesign (handoff `/tank/handoffs/cyrus/cyrus-handoff/`, START-HERE.md) replaces the v4 studio at **`/dashboard/cyrus`** (+ `/dashboard/cyrus/[id]`, and the core gallery at **`/dashboard/cyrus/cores`**). Same preview gate (`requireModBuilderUser()` on every page, `modBuilderUser()` on every API). The portal sidebar and top bar stay; the studio fills the app frame.

**Where it lives.** UI `components/cyrus/{chrome,cosmos,cores,icons,preview,prompt}` + `CyrusApp.tsx` (handoff components, imports re-rooted); state/engine `lib/cyrus/{store,forge,fx,data,types,camera,hooks,zip,highlight}.ts` + `lib/cyrus/engine/` (template generators); game logos `public/cyrus/games/`. Kept from v4: `components/cyrus/kit/` (icon set used by the token modal, the install-to-server modal), `lib/cyrus/{projects,meta,models,estimate,uploads,diff,tokens/}`.

**Scoping (nothing leaks into the portal).** `app/dashboard/cyrus/layout.tsx` wraps every Cyrus route in `.cyrus-root.nx-dark-island` and loads Inter / Space Grotesk / JetBrains Mono as CSS variables on that box only. `studio.css` (handoff globals + network CSS) and `cores/cores.css` are generated from the handoff with every selector under `.cyrus-root`, keyframes and `@property` renamed `cy5-*`, and the three class names that collide with portal globals renamed (`cy5-glass`, `cy5-btn-ghost`, `cy5-kbd`). The root uses `container-type: size; contain: layout paint`, so the handoff's `position: fixed` chrome is contained in the content area; `100vw/vh` became `cqw/cqh`. Tailwind colour tokens are `cy-*` (`text-cy-ink`, `border-cy-line` …, `@theme inline` in `app/globals.css` pointing at variables that exist only on `.cyrus-root`), plus a `cy-light:` variant. `nx-dark-island` keeps the portal's generated light-mode retargeting off the studio (it has its own light theme). `test/cyrus.test.ts` fails if a studio selector is unscoped or a keyframe isn't `cy5-`.

**Theme.** The portal's: `html[data-theme="light"]` / localStorage `nx-theme`. The studio's toggle presses the portal's own toggle button; `useCyrusBoot` mirrors `data-theme` into the store for the canvas and shaders. No `cyrus-theme` key.

**Real vs template.** Minecraft is the one real game (`GAMES[].real`). The account's builds are its Minecraft mods (`lib/cyrus/real.ts deriveReal`: one mod per project, builds = versions, category from the build's own words, at most two extra category branches). Minecraft seeds are dashed **ideas**: clicking one writes a buildable prompt. Notes / restore / favourite are the existing `PATCH /api/mod-builder/projects/:root`; files load lazily from `/api/mod-builder/builds/:id/source`; downloads are the real `.jar` / source zip; **Deploy** opens the v4 install modal. Every other game (and added games) is the handoff's template generator, labelled "Template preview", spends no tokens, kept in localStorage per account (`cyrus-state-v1:<userId>`).

**Forge stream** (`POST /api/cyrus/generate`, NDJSON, handoff §6 GenEvents). A prompt that routes to Minecraft, or a change to a real mod, goes through `lib/modbuilder/create.ts createModBuild` (extracted from `POST /api/mod-builder/builds`, which now calls it too: same validation, rate limits, 2-in-flight cap and token gate); token errors answer JSON 402/403/429 before the stream so `cyrusTokens.handleBuildError` opens the modal. Then `lib/cyrus/follow.ts` streams the real build: stage changes → `think`, the service `/live` draft → `file`/`chunk`, in-place edits → `file-set`, keep-alive `ping`, final source + `done {tokens: charged}` or `error`. `GET ?follow=<id>` re-attaches (page load with a running build, dropped connection; the client retries 4×). Template games run the handoff's `forgeStream()` (no model call). Additive event types: `build`, `file-set`, `ping`.

**Tokens** (UI-CONTRACT.md): `<CyrusTokensHost/>` in `CyrusApp`; `<CyrusTokenChip compact/>` replaces the handoff's credit counter in the top bar; `<CyrusTokenEstimate/>` in the prompt dock for real targets; `<CyrusModelLock/>` + typical token range per model + `<CyrusModelPanelFoot/>` in the model picker; `cyrusTokens.refresh()` after each real build. The local `credits` counter is gone. Model ids/names stay the economy's: Katara / Saka / Yakko.

**Verification** (node-2, devhost): throwaway DB seeded by `.cyrus-verify/seed.ts` (not committed), a local stand-in of the build service (`.cyrus-verify/mock-svc.mjs`, same HTTP as the VM; the portal's real create/sync/live/source/jar code runs unchanged), Playwright screenshots in `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-redesign/shots/`.

content.thinking:
While waiting, I'm mentally reviewing my generator code for logic errors, checking how the effects body handles per-key world effects and empty server effect cases to make sure the generated function bodies stay valid.

I check through weapon categories using only local effects, confirming Commands.hit and Effects.hit wire together correctly, then trace how Config and MOD_ID get defined and referenced across lite versus full modes for Actions, Effects, and client files.

Then I hit a real concern: in lite mode, the shared Main.lua requires a server-folder file (Items/ProceduralDistributions) inside an `if not isClient()` check, but that server subfolder only loads when a save is launched — not at main menu startup when shared code first runs — so this require could fail in single-player at the title screen.

I reason through PZ's load order: Lua reloads on exit/launch of a save, server files load when launching a save, so events registered at startup persist into the save. Since ProceduralDistributions is only actually used inside the OnPreDistributionMerge handler, which fires later during save load after server files are loaded, the top-level require is unnecessary and should be removed in lite mode while kept in the full server file.

Then I notice a subtler issue: on an MP client at the main menu, isServer() is true but isClient() is false before connecting, so the lite "server" block would wrongly execute client-side logic until Lua reloads after joining a server. I need to confirm whether Lua actually reloads on connecting to MP to resolve this.

I'm wondering if registering server-side logic in a different event like OnServerStarted would avoid the ambiguity, but that doesn't cover singleplayer startup either. Checking how the full version structures this, it seems the server files are only loaded at save/server launch time, so an isClient() guard then is reliable in a way lite's unified loading can't replicate.

Given lite's three-file limit, I'm considering placing the lite Main.lua inside the server lua folder instead of shared, since that folder loads correctly in singleplayer, dedicated servers, and even MP clients according to the loading table I reviewed — all at the point where isClient()/isServer() resolve accurately, which would make this placement work everywhere despite some timing caveats.

But the validator's rule for timed actions insists they live in shared, which conflicts with putting a lite action-based file in server/ — even though server-loaded files would technically function there too. That contradiction makes me think I need a simpler fallback approach for the lite template's file placement.

Actually, maybe it's cleaner to push the isClient() check inside each event handler rather than guarding registration itself, since that evaluates accurately at runtime. The top-level setup code in the server script (zone tables, loot defs) is harmless to run on clients too, so I could just rewrite each `Events.X.Add(fn)` call to wrap the handler with a server-only guard.

I'm also checking that requiring a client-only vanilla file from the shared load phase could be risky, since load order puts shared mod code before client vanilla files load, so an early require might cause issues even if it technically succeeds.

I should strip those requires from the lite client block since the code only references them inside runtime handlers anyway, so they aren't needed at load time. The shared-vanilla require for ISBaseTimedAction is safe since vanilla shared files load before mod shared files, and the full-mode Actions/Client requires between shared and client paths within the same mod are also fine since they're already loaded by the time they're referenced.

Checking a few more spots: the Effects shared file loading on clients is harmless since it's just definitions, Server.lua's require of Effects/Config shared is fine too, and `allow()` using player:getUsername() works correctly in singleplayer. The router's distance check and reward command logic look consistent, and the Trade action's validity check, server rebuild, and client power-based perform calls all appear to be wired correctly.

Now I'm checking vehicle boost requests, which default to the player target fine. For interface/audio/shaders, effects stay disabled appropriately since no Effects file is used client-side. For mechanics though, I'm noticing a semantic issue: Effects.hit now applies "foe" effects onto the player itself as source, matching the original client logic, but the world effects (like fire) used to trigger at a ring square 10-25 tiles away from the mechanics event, whereas now they're applying directly at the target's current square — that's a behavioral change I need to flag.

I should give Effects.hit an optional square parameter so world effects can target a ring square around the player instead of under their feet, then update the mechanics and world pulse calls to pass in that ringSquare value while weapon/item effects keep using the target's actual square. Summons at a ring square and periodic foe effects (like poison) during mechanics pulses remain consistent with the original design, and I'm now checking the character guard logic where self-effects apply through Effects.hit for zombies/NPCs.

I realize the quest reward is broken though — applying foe effects to the player as a "reward" makes no sense, since the original design was self effects on the player plus foe/world effects on nearby zombies. The fix is to split Effects.hit into Effects.onSelf (just self effects) and Effects.onTarget (foe+world effects), so quests can call onSelf once for the player and loop onTarget across nearby zombies instead of misapplying foe effects to the reward recipient.

I need to restructure the whole Effects API into separate self/foe/world functions, with hit() as a composite that calls all three — otherwise item release logic ends up firing world effects (like lightning) once per zombie instead of once at the nearest square, and self effects get duplicated per zombie hit.

For each caller I'm mapping which args go where: creature abilities use hit(player, zombie, power, zombie's square) so world effects land on the zombie's tile; vehicle ramming applies foe per zombie but only one world effect at the nearest zombie; world zones and pulses pass the ring square explicitly so foe/self land on the player while world effects stay anchored to the zone geometry.

Quests just need self(player) plus a foe application to nearby zombies, so now I can write the effectsBody functions matching each of these patterns.

I need to figure out how to include the UI class definitions in lite's Main.lua without breaking load order, since ISPanel-derived classes can't be defined until vanilla client UI classes have loaded.

So maybe the cleanest fix is to split lite into separate Client.lua and Server.lua files, each inlining the shared config/effects they need, and placing UI code in the client file and reward/server logic in the server file — though this then raises the question of how to handle categories needing shared action files, which may require a fourth file for lite setups involving items and actions.

I need to drop the self-reference requires like `"${cls}/HUD"` from Client.lua in the lite split, since those files won't exist there, keeping the lite path capped at Client.lua, optional Server.lua, and mod.info. Time to start implementing this.

name=poison fire summon
id=PoisonFireSummon
author=Cyrus
description=Weapon mod. Sets targets ablaze. Tune it under Sandbox Options > poison fire summon.
category=features
modversion=2.0
versionMin=42.15
--[[
    poison fire summon · client
    Weapons mod for Project Zomboid Build 42 (42.15+) · forged by Cyrus (Saka) v2
]]
-- v2: retuned defaults; every number now lives in sandbox options
local Config = require("PoisonFireSummon/Config")
local MOD = Config.MOD_ID

local ITEM = "PoisonFireSummon.PoisonFireSummon"
local function state(obj)
    local md = obj:getModData()
    md[MOD] = md[MOD] or {}
    return md[MOD]
end

--- Game-state changes are the server's job in Build 42; in singleplayer the command loops straight back.
local function request(player, command, target, extra)
    local args = extra or {}
    target = target or player
    args.x, args.y, args.z = math.floor(target:getX()), math.floor(target:getY()), math.floor(target:getZ())
    if instanceof(target, "IsoZombie") then args.zid = target:getOnlineID() end
    sendClientCommand(player, MOD, command, args)
end

--- Zombie hit by a local player's swing: a cheap client pre-check, the server decides and applies.
Events.OnHitZombie.Add(function(zombie, attacker, bodyPart, weapon)
    if not weapon or weapon:getFullType() ~= ITEM or not Config.get("Enabled") then return end
    if not instanceof(attacker, "IsoPlayer") or not attacker:isLocalPlayer() then return end

if isClient() then return end

require "Items/ProceduralDistributions"
local Config = require("PoisonFireSummon/Config")
local Effects = require("PoisonFireSummon/Effects")
local MOD = Config.MOD_ID

-- Container list -> base weight per roll (vanilla tools sit around 1-10).
local LOOT = { GarageTools = 1.0, CrateTools = 0.6, ToolStoreTools = 0.3 }

Events.OnPreDistributionMerge.Add(function()
    for list, weight in pairs(LOOT) do
        local dist = ProceduralDistributions.list[list]
        if dist and dist.items then
            table.insert(dist.items, "PoisonFireSummon.PoisonFireSummon")
            table.insert(dist.items, weight * Config.get("LootWeight"))
        end
    end
end)

local Commands = {}
local last = {}

--- Server-side rate limit per player and action, so a modified client cannot spam effects.
local function allow(player, action, seconds)
    local key, now = player:getUsername() .. ":" .. action, getTimestampMs()
    if last[key] and now - last[key] < seconds * 1000 then return false end
    last[key] = now
    return true
end

--- Bonus damage on every hit, scaled by the weapon's condition; the special effect on a server-side roll.
function Commands.hit(player, args)
    local weapon = player:getPrimaryHandItem()
    if not weapon or weapon:getFullType() ~= "PoisonFireSummon.PoisonFireSummon" or not allow(player, "hit", 0.2) then return end
    local zombie = Effects.findZombie(args.x, args.y, args.z, args.zid)
    if not zombie or zombie:DistTo(player) > 3 then return end
    local power = Config.scaled(Config.get("Power"), weapon:getCondition(), weapon:getConditionMax())
    zombie:setHealth(zombie:getHealth() - power * 0.02)
    if ZombRandFloat(0, 1) <= Config.get("Chance") and allow(player, "proc", Config.get("Cooldown")) then
        Effects.hit(zombie, player, power)
    end
end

Events.OnClientCommand.Add(function(module, command, player, args)
    if module ~= MOD or not Commands[command] or type(args) ~= "table" or not Config.get("Enabled") then return end
    -- never trust a client blindly: whatever it points at has to be near the sender
    if not args.x or not args.y or IsoUtils.DistanceTo(player:getX(), player:getY(), args.x, args.y) > 30 then return end
    Commands[command](player, args)
end)
--[[
    poison fire summon · effects: only ever called on the server (or in singleplayer)
    Weapons mod for Project Zomboid Build 42 (42.15+) · forged by Cyrus (Saka) v2
]]
-- v2: retuned defaults; every number now lives in sandbox options
local Config = require("PoisonFireSummon/Config")

local Effects = { Fx = {}, WorldFx = {} }
local Fx, WorldFx = Effects.Fx, Effects.WorldFx

--- Fire only outdoors, away from buildings, water and safehouses, and only while the server allows it.
local function canBurn(square)
    if not Config.get("AllowFire") or not square:isOutside() or square:getBuilding() or square:isWaterSquare() or square:haveFire() then return false end
    return not (SafeHouse and SafeHouse.getSafeHouse(square))
end

--- B42 stats: getStats():add(CharacterStat.X, delta). A fraction of the stat's range; a no-op if the stat is missing.
local function nudge(character, name, fraction)
    local stat = CharacterStat and CharacterStat[name]
    if not stat then return end
    character:getStats():add(stat, (stat:getMaximumValue() - stat:getMinimumValue()) * fraction)
end

local function hurt(zombie, amount, source)
    zombie:setHealth(zombie:getHealth() - amount)
    if zombie:getHealth() <= 0 then zombie:Kill(source) end
end

--- Sets targets ablaze
function WorldFx.fire(square, source, power)
    if canBurn(square) then
        IsoFireManager.StartFire(square:getCell(), square, true, math.floor(60 + power * 4))
    end
end

--- Poisons on hit
function Fx.poison(target, source, power)
    if instanceof(target, "IsoPlayer") then
        nudge(target, "POISON", 0.02 * power)
    else
        hurt(target, power * 0.02, source)
    end
end

--- The zombie a client pointed at: matched by online ID when there is one, else the nearest within 2 tiles.
function Effects.findZombie(x, y, z, zid)
    local best, bestDist
    for dx = -2, 2 do
        for dy = -2, 2 do
            local square = getCell():getGridSquare(x + dx, y + dy, z)
            local movers = square and square:getMovingObjects()
            for i = 0, movers and movers:size() - 1 or -1 do
                local obj = movers:get(i)
                if instanceof(obj, "IsoZombie") and not obj:isDead() then
                    if zid and zid >= 0 and obj:getOnlineID() == zid then return obj end
                    local dist = IsoUtils.DistanceTo(x, y, obj:getX(), obj:getY())
                    if not bestDist or dist < bestDist then best, bestDist = obj, dist end
                end
            end
        end
    end
    return best
end

--- Foe effects on one target, self effects on the source, world effects on one square. Area callers use them separately.
function Effects.foe(target, source, power)
    Fx.poison(target, source, power)
end
function Effects.self(who, power)
end
function Effects.world(square, source, power)
    if not square then return end
    WorldFx.fire(square, source, power)
end
--- One proc: everything at once; world effects at `square` (default: the target's square).
function Effects.hit(target, source, power, square)
    Effects.foe(target, source, power)
    Effects.self(source, power)
    Effects.world(square or target:getCurrentSquare(), source, power)
end

return Effects

--[[
    poison fire summon · timed actions (shared: the server runs complete())
    Characters mod for Project Zomboid Build 42 (42.15+) · forged by Cyrus (Yakko) v2
]]
-- v2: retuned defaults; every number now lives in sandbox options
require "TimedActions/ISBaseTimedAction"
local Config = require("PoisonFireSummon/Config")
local Effects = require("PoisonFireSummon/Effects")
local MOD = Config.MOD_ID

local GOODS = { "Base.Lighter", "Base.Hat_GasMask", "Base.TinnedBeans" }

ISPoisonFireSummonTrade = ISBaseTimedAction:derive("ISPoisonFireSummonTrade")

--- The price is worked out where it is used, never passed in, so a client cannot set its own.
local function price(character) return Config.price(Config.get("Price"), character:getZombieKills()) end

function ISPoisonFireSummonTrade:isValid()
    if self.npc and self.npc:isDead() then return false end
    return self.character:getInventory():getCountTypeRecurse("Base.Money") >= price(self.character)
end

function ISPoisonFireSummonTrade:update() if self.npc then self.character:faceThisObject(self.npc) end end
function ISPoisonFireSummonTrade:start() if self.npc then self.npc:Say(getTextOrNull("IGUI_PoisonFireSummon_Greet") or "Show me what you've got.") end end
function ISPoisonFireSummonTrade:stop() ISBaseTimedAction.stop(self) end

function ISPoisonFireSummonTrade:waitToStart()
    if not self.npc then return false end
    self.character:faceThisObject(self.npc)
    return self.character:shouldBeTurning()
end

function ISPoisonFireSummonTrade:perform()
    local md = self.character:getModData()
    md[MOD] = md[MOD] or {}
    md[MOD].lastTrade = getGameTime():getWorldAgeHours()
    ISBaseTimedAction.perform(self)
end

--- Server and SP: the bills go, the goods arrive, and both are synced to the player's client.
function ISPoisonFireSummonTrade:complete()
    local inv = self.character:getInventory()
    for _ = 1, price(self.character) do
        local bill = inv:getFirstTypeRecurse("Base.Money")
        if not bill then return false end
        local from = bill:getContainer()
        from:Remove(bill)
        sendRemoveItemFromContainer(from, bill)
    end
    for _, fullType in ipairs(GOODS) do
        local item = instanceItem(fullType)
        if item then
            inv:AddItem(item)
            sendAddItemToContainer(inv, item)
        end
    end
    return true
end

function ISPoisonFireSummonTrade:getDuration() return self.character:isTimedActionInstant() and 1 or 133 end

function ISPoisonFireSummonTrade:new(character)
    local o = ISBaseTimedAction.new(self, character)
    o.stopOnWalk, o.stopOnRun = true, true
    o.maxTime = o:getDuration()
    return o
end
=====
-- client and singleplayer ------------------------------------------------
if not isServer() then
    local active = false
    local function txt(key, fallback) return getTextOrNull("IGUI_FrostLightningWeapon_" .. key) or fallback end

    local function eachLocalPlayer(fn)
        for i = 0, getNumActivePlayers() - 1 do
            local player = getSpecificPlayer(i)
            if player and not player:isDead() then fn(player) end
        end
    end

    local function alarm(player)
        getSoundManager():PlayWorldSound("FrostLightningWeapon_Alarm", player:getCurrentSquare(), 0, 150, 1.0, false)
    end

    Events.OnServerCommand.Add(function(module, command, args)
        if module ~= MOD then return end
        if command == "start" then
            active = true
            eachLocalPlayer(function(player)
                player:setHaloNote(string.format(txt("Start", "Night %d. It begins."), args.night), 255, 70, 50, 600)
                alarm(player)
            end)
        elseif command == "pulse" and active then
            eachLocalPlayer(function(player)
                alarm(player)
            end)
        elseif command == "stop" then
            active = false
            eachLocalPlayer(function(player) player:setHaloNote(txt("Stop", "It's over. For now."), 120, 220, 120, 400) end)
        end
    end)
end

-- server and singleplayer ------------------------------------------------
-- A shared file loads before a multiplayer client knows it is one, so each handler checks when it fires.
local function onServer(event, fn) Events[event].Add(function(...) if not isClient() then return fn(...) end end) end
local function forEachPlayer(fn)
    local online = isServer() and getOnlinePlayers()
    for i = 0, online and online:size() - 1 or getNumActivePlayers() - 1 do
        local player = online and online:get(i) or getSpecificPlayer(i)
        if player and not player:isDead() then fn(player) end
    end
end

--- A free outdoor square on a ring around (x, y), or nil after a few tries.
local function ringSquare(x, y, minDist, maxDist)
    for _ = 1, 16 do
        local angle, dist = ZombRandFloat(0, math.pi * 2), ZombRandFloat(minDist, maxDist)
        local square = getCell():getGridSquare(math.floor(x + math.cos(angle) * dist), math.floor(y + math.sin(angle) * dist), 0)
        if square and square:isFree(false) and square:isOutside() then return square end
    end
end

--- sendServerCommand only reaches clients on a dedicated server; in singleplayer fire the same client event locally.
local function notify(player, command, args)
    if isServer() then
        if player then sendServerCommand(player, MOD, command, args) else sendServerCommand(MOD, command, args) end
    else
        triggerEvent("OnServerCommand", MOD, command, args)
    end
end

local function data() return ModData.getOrCreate(MOD) end

local function startEvent(night)
    local d = data()
    d.active, d.night = true, night
    d.endsAt = getGameTime():getWorldAgeHours() + Config.get("Duration")
    notify(nil, "start", { night = night })
    print(string.format("[%s] night %d: event started", MOD, night))
end

onServer("EveryHours", function()
    local gt, d = getGameTime(), data()
    if not Config.get("Enabled") then return end
    if d.active then
        if gt:getWorldAgeHours() >= d.endsAt then
            d.active, d.lastNight = false, d.night
            notify(nil, "stop", { night = d.night })
        end
        return
    end
    local night = gt:getNightsSurvived()
    if gt:getHour() == Config.get("StartHour") and d.lastNight ~= night and Config.isEventNight(night, Config.get("Interval")) then
        startEvent(night)
    end
end)

onServer("EveryTenMinutes", function()
    if not data().active then return end
    local power = Config.get("Power")
    forEachPlayer(function(player)
        Effects.hit(player, player, power, ringSquare(player:getX(), player:getY(), 10, 25))
    end)
    notify(nil, "pulse", {})
end)

input.message:
**game-zomboid: done.** Branch `feature/cyrus-v6-game-zomboid`, worktree `/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-v6-game-zomboid`. Commit `ef7a46c2c8`, which sits on a fast-forward of `feature/cyrus-v6` (the knowledge-field commit `687e055065`). Nothing deployed or merged to main. The game is still `soon`.

**Verified on node-2:** `tsc --noEmit` reported no errors. `test/cyrus-game-zomboid.test.ts` passed 21/21. I also generated 216 mods (12 archetypes × 3 models × 6 prompts) and ran the validator on all of them: zero blocking issues. The only warnings are the expected ones for per-frame handlers and `ModData.transmit`. No mod has been loaded in a real game.

**What I built**
- `lib/cyrus/games/zomboid.ts`: the `GameSupport` (default export) plus `PZ_TARGET` (folder `42`, versionMin 42.15, tested on 42.21).
  - Version table: 42.21 current; 42.15–42.20 supported; 42.13–42.14 and 41.78 unsupported.
  - Install side is `both`, with customer-facing reason/clientNote text. Nxeon's `b42`/`b41` variants are reflected: Cyrus mods only work on `b42` servers.
  - 17 dangerous-API rules, breakage risks, outdated signals, categories using the routing agent's 16 universal ids, sources and unknowns.
  - The new `knowledge` field: 14 API-sheet lines and 12 Build 41 → 42 failure rules with regex detectors.
- `lib/cyrus/engine/games/zomboid.ts`: generator rewritten for 42.15+ and the 42.13 multiplayer rules.
  - The game server owns all game-state changes. Clients only send requests; the server checks distance, cooldowns and what the player holds.
  - Timed actions moved to `shared` with `getDuration()`/`complete()`; items are created on the server and synced.
  - JSON translations, `ItemType` and registry ids, an own script module, per-mod Lua folders.
  - Fire only starts outdoors, never in buildings or safehouses, and only while `AllowFire` is on. Map files are gone. Missing art and sounds are listed in `ASSETS.md`.
  - Removed calls replaced: the old per-stat getters/setters, `setRunSpeedModifier`, `getNumMoodles`, `setLx`, `square:Is`, `Type =`/`DisplayName`, `.txt` translations.
  - Katara drafts are 3 files at most and always include `mod.info`.
- `lib/cyrus/games/zomboid.validate.ts`: `validateZomboidMod()` checks layout, `mod.info`, Lua 5.1 structure (my own TypeScript lexer), dangerous APIs, the failure rules, the multiplayer rules, script braces and JSON translations.
- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` has a new "Cyrus v6: Project Zomboid support" section.
- Notes in `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-v6/game-zomboid/`: `API-CHECK.md` (every API checked, and what was removed or replaced) and `READINESS.md` (go-live checklist plus a 1-page "how Zomboid modding works" explainer for marketing).

**Your messages**
- Merged `feature/cyrus-v6` and filled in `knowledge` with verified facts only.
- Read the Zomboid section of ADVANCED-MODS.md. The `Mods=` backslash conflict is settled by The Indie Stone's own 42.15 migration guide: plain MOD_IDs, with the old `\` form still accepted. It still needs a real-server test, which is in `unknowns` and READINESS.
- Nxeon's real build: the image runs with `SERVER_BRANCH=` empty, so the public branch, which is 42.21 today. The panel's default variant is `b42`, and `b41` Legacy also exists.
- pzwiki: before your message I had pulled a few raw pzwiki pages with `curl` (WebFetch got a 403). I stopped once you flagged it. Every shipped fact is re-sourced to the Steam news API, the TIS migration guides (archived on GitHub), the Modding Policy, PZ-API-Docs, the 42.21 JavaDocs, LuaDocs, Umbrella and the B42 guide on GitHub. pzwiki is cited nowhere; `API-CHECK.md` says this too.

**Load-test harness:** not implemented, so `verification.method` stays `static-lint`. A real test would download the free PZ dedicated server (app 380870, SteamCMD anonymous) into a sandbox container, boot it with the mod, and scan `console.txt` for Lua errors. Nothing proprietary would need to be stored or redistributed, but it needs a sandbox VM with about 4–6 GB RAM. Running the generated Lua unit tests also needs a Lua 5.1 interpreter, which isn't installed anywhere. Exact steps are in READINESS.md.

**Outside my files:** nothing changed. The registry `lib/cyrus/games.ts` (`CYRUS_GAMES`) has no zomboid row, so whoever owns the "add game" limit (studio-ui) needs to add `{ id: "zomboid", status: "soon", ... }` if Zomboid should appear there.

**Main unknowns:** whether `CharacterStat` is reachable from Lua (the code is guarded so it degrades to a no-op), whether OnHitZombie fires on the client or the server, whether server-side stat and walk-type changes sync to players, `triggerEvent` in singleplayer, and server loading of a mod from the local `mods/` folder.

**Decisions for the owner**
1. When to wire Zomboid into the real AI build service: generate, run the validator, repair, then show.
2. Whether to approve a sandbox VM for real load tests.
3. How players get the files. Steam Workshop is the only automatic route, and it needs the creator's own Steam account; Nxeon can't upload for them. The alternative is a manual "server pack" download.
4. The Modding Policy forbids selling access to mods, so community and store Zomboid mods must stay free and credit any forks.
5. The lifecycle flow must refuse to install Cyrus mods on `b41` servers.
